slides.title: London
slides.titleZh: 雾都漫步 · 探秘大伦敦
slides.tagline: 乘坐红色双层巴士，感受泰晤士河畔的大本钟与塔桥！
slides.intro: 伦敦是世界上历史最悠久、文化最多元的国际大都市之一，这里不仅有大本钟、白金汉宫，还有古老的红色双层巴士和地铁！
slides.contentEn:
It is one of the largest and most cosmopolitan cities in the world and has over 9 million inhabitants. London is in the southeast of England. The River Thames separates the North and South Banks. There are 32 boroughs as well as the City, the heart of London. This centre of 2.6 square miles comprises of offices, banks, the Houses of Parliament and Big Ben, Westminster Abbey and Buckingham Palace.
London has red double-decker buses, black taxicabs and the Tube - the oldest underground in the world. Tourist and cultural attractions include many parks such as Hyde Park and Regents Park, museums such as the National Gallery and the British Museum, and monuments such as the Tower of London and Tower Bridge. If you want to go to the theatre, opera or the pub, you have many to choose from!
slides.contentZh: 伦敦是世界上最大、最多元化的大都市之一，拥有超过900万居民。伦敦位于英格兰东南部，蜿蜒的泰晤士河将城市划分为南岸与北岸。伦敦拥有32个自治市以及被称为城市心脏的'伦敦城'。在这片充满活力的市中心，汇集着议会大厦、大本钟、西敏寺和白金汉宫。伦敦标志性的红色双层巴士、黑色出租车以及世界上历史最悠久的地铁（The Tube）随处可见。海德公园、国家美术馆、大英博物馆、伦敦塔与塔桥等世界名胜引人入胜。在这里，精彩的戏剧、歌剧与传统英式餐厅随时向你敞开大门！

quiz.question: What is the world's oldest underground railway in London called? (伦敦历史最悠久的地铁被称为什么？)
quiz.explanation: 太聪明啦！伦敦地铁是全世界第一条地下铁道，当地人亲切地称它为'The Tube'（管道）！

slides.title: Canterbury
slides.titleZh: 中世纪回响 · 坎特伯雷古城
slides.tagline: 漫步千年大教堂与罗马古城墙，聆听朝圣者的古老故事！
slides.intro: 坎特伯雷是英国基督教的摇篮，这里的坎特伯雷大教堂以绚丽的彩色玻璃和诺曼式雕塑闻名于世。
slides.contentEn:
It is best known for having the country's first cathedral which was founded by Saint Augustine when he arrived from Rome in 597 AD. Canterbury Cathedral, rebuilt during the 11th to 12th centuries and the 14th to 15th centuries, is the home of the Anglican church. It is particularly admired for its Norman architectural sculpture and beautiful stained glass windows.
It was in this cathedral that the Archbishop Thomas à Becket was murdered in 1170. Following this event, Canterbury became a place of pilgrimage as pilgrims travelled for miles to visit Becket's shrine. 
Canterbury has continued to be a major tourist site as visitors come to admire the numerous areas of historic interest. These include the remains of the city wall originally built by the Romans, the remains of Saint Augustine's Abbey and, of course, the cathedral, which dominates the city's skyline.
slides.contentZh: 坎特伯雷以拥有英国第一座大教堂而享誉世界，该教堂由圣奥古斯丁于公元597年自罗马抵达后创建。坎特伯雷大教堂在11至15世纪经历了数次宏伟重建，是英国圣公会的母堂，其典雅的诺曼式建筑雕塑和璀璨的彩色花窗玻璃令人叹为观止。历史上，这里曾是欧洲最著名的朝圣圣地之一，无数朝圣者千里跋涉只为探访古迹。如今，坎特伯雷依然是世界游客的必游之地，城中留存着古罗马人建造的古老城墙、圣奥古斯丁修道院遗址以及高耸入云的宏伟教堂。

quiz.question: When was the first cathedral in Canterbury founded? (坎特伯雷第一座大教堂建于哪一年？)
quiz.explanation: 答对啦！公元 597 年圣奥古斯丁来到这里创建了第一座教堂，距今已有 1400 多年历史啦！

slides.title: The Angel of the North
slides.titleZh: 巨型钢铁奇迹 · 北方天使之翼
slides.tagline: 高达20米、展翅54米的现代巨型雕塑，守护英格兰北方！
slides.intro: 由雕塑大师安东尼·葛姆雷设计的'北方天使'，用200吨钢铁伫立在山丘上，张开双翼迎候往来旅人。
slides.contentEn: It was erected in 1997 in the northeast of England. It is twenty metres high, it weighs one hundred tonnes and its wingspan is fifty-two metres (almost the same as a jumbo jet). Constructed with scrap car metal, this sculpture was designed by the artist Antony Gormley, a past winner of the Turner Prize. The hilltop site where it now stands, in Gateshead just outside Newcastle, is considered to be of symbolic importance as it is the location of former coal mines. Those who object to the sculpture have attacked it for being 'illogical' and 'ridiculous'. Nevertheless, the angel, which is visible from a distance of thirty miles, is rapidly becoming one of the great visual symbols of the North of England.
slides.contentZh: '北方天使'是当代英国最著名的大型户外雕塑之一。这座由著名雕塑家安东尼·葛姆雷创作的钢铁巨像高达20米，双翼展开达54米，比一架波音747客机还要宽广！它矗立在一座俯瞰交通要道的小山丘上，由200吨耐候钢制造而成，能够抵御每小时超过100英里的强风。它不仅象征着英格兰北部工业文明的坚韧历史，更像一位温柔的天使，默默张开怀抱守护着每一位旅人与回家的人。

quiz.question: How wide is the wingspan of the Angel of the North? (北方天使的翼展有多宽？)
quiz.explanation: 太厉害啦！北方天使展翅达到 54 米，甚至比波音 747 飞机的机翼还要宽大！

slides.title: The Turner Prize
slides.titleZh: 环球探索 · The Turner Prize
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 The Turner Prize 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 探索英国及国际经典人文胜地，拓展少儿跨文化视野。
slides.contentEn:
It was created in 1984 with a prize of £20,000 in cash. The Turner Prize is famous for controversy. Some critics argue that it promotes public discussion in contemporary British art. Others, however, argue that it is intentionally controversial, and ruins art's reputation.
One of the early winners of the prize, Damien Hirst, became famous for his exhibit of a pickled cow in 1995. Later exhibits have been just as original. They include an unmade bed and a pile of rice! 
British contemporary art can claim that the 1990s was its most productive era, with artists such as Damien Hirst and Tracey Emin producing many famous exhibits. The decade ended with the construction of the Tate Modern Museum in London. To reflect the originality of British contemporary art, this museum was converted from an old power station!

slides.title: John Constable
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 John Constable 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 探索英国及国际经典人文胜地，拓展少儿跨文化视野。
slides.contentEn:
He was born on June 11th 1776 in Suffolk, England. He loved the country scenes of Suffolk and it was this that inspired him to paint. Among Constable's most famous works are the paintings 'The Hay-Wain', 'Stratford Mill' and 'The Lock', all of which are scenes from the village where he grew up. 
Constable worked hard for many years in an attempt to paint realistic representations of country scenes. He finally achieved this by turning from the conventions of 18th century landscape painting and concentrating on the changing effects of light and colour that occur in nature.
When Constable died on March 31st 1837, his reputation was limited. Since his death, however, the admiration of his work has grown considerably. He is now greatly admired for his fresh and genuine representation of English landscape.

slides.title: The Union Jack
slides.titleZh: 米字旗的秘密 · 联合王国之旗
slides.tagline: 探秘由三面十字旗融合而成的米字旗（Union Jack）！
slides.intro: 英国国旗为什么长成这样？原来它巧妙融合了英格兰、苏格兰与爱尔兰三个守护圣人的十字标志！
slides.contentEn:
It is so called because it represents a union of countries -  England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales - united under one Sovereign. The origin of 'Jack' is uncertain.
The correct name for the flag, although rarely used, is the Union Flag. It includes the Crosses of St. George (England), St. Andrew (Scotland), and St. Patrick (Ireland).
In 1606, the first flag of Great Britain was created and included the red perpendicular cross of England and the white diagonal cross of Scotland on a blue background. This flag was used from 1606 through to 1801. At this point Ireland became officially united with England and the Irish Cross, a red diagonal cross on white, was added to the flag. The Union Jack has remained the same ever since.
slides.contentZh: 英国国旗通常被称为'联合杰克'（Union Jack），它是英国历史演进的生动缩影。这面旗帜由三个古老历史王国守护圣人的十字旗帜精妙交织而成：英格兰守护圣人圣乔治的红十字、苏格兰守护圣人圣安德鲁的白斜十字，以及爱尔兰守护圣人圣帕特里克的红斜十字。自1801年正式确立以来，米字旗已成为世界上最著名且极具辨识度的旗帜之一，代表着大不列颠与北爱尔兰联合王国的深厚历史底蕴。

quiz.question: What is the British national flag commonly known as? (英国国旗通常被称为什么？)
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！英国国旗被亲切地称为'Union Jack'（联合杰克），象征着联合王国！

slides.title: Tea
slides.titleZh: 香浓下午茶 · 英国红茶文化
slides.tagline: 配上一块香甜司康饼，体验精致惬意的英式茶歇时光！
slides.intro: 英国人每天喝掉数千万杯茶！红茶搭配鲜奶与点心，是英国人一天中最温暖放松的生活仪式。
slides.contentEn:
It's strange to think that tea came to Britain as a medicine in the 17th century. The upper classes, especially women, were the first people to drink tea socially. In the 19th century, low prices and increased trade with India and Sri Lanka meant that tea became widely available. Indeed, for many working-class families, tea became an integral part of the evening meal. This meal was known as 'High Tea'.
However, tea is known principally as an afternoon drink. This may originate from 19th-century tea dances, held at 5 o'clock in the afternoon. People came to eat cakes and sandwiches, dance, and of course, drink tea. The dances may not still take place, but the practice of afternoon tea and cakes is as British as the Union Jack!
slides.contentZh: 在英国，饮茶不仅是一种生活习惯，更是一门传承百年的社交艺术。英国人每天要喝掉大约1.65亿杯茶！传统的英式下午茶（Afternoon Tea）起源于19世纪，由贝德福德第七任公爵夫人安娜发明。在悠闲的午后，一壶热气腾腾的伯爵红茶或大吉岭红茶，注入一小勺新鲜牛奶，再搭配涂着浓缩奶油与草莓酱的英式司康饼（Scones）或黄瓜三明治，惬意非凡！

quiz.question: What sweet treat is typically served with afternoon tea? (英式下午茶通常搭配哪种经典小点心？)
quiz.explanation: 真棒！刚出炉的司康饼涂上凝脂奶油与果酱，是英式红茶的最佳黄金搭档！

slides.title: The British Pub
slides.titleZh: 环球探索 · The British Pub
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 The British Pub 的精彩故事！

slides.contentEn:
Pubs play a very important role in the lives of British people and have served as meeting places for centuries. Not only can we drink a wide selection of beverages but also eat, play games, and socialise. This is why a pub is very often the central aspect of even the smallest villages.
Pubs may be found in all sorts of buildings and locations. For example, there are renovated castles, country houses, city pubs, and even pubs in the middle of nowhere! One thing that they nearly all have in common is that they have two bars. You can choose between the public bar and the lounge bar. 
Often pubs have a garden for sitting outside in the summer and a log fire for winter evenings. Look out for the wonderful pub names, such as 'The Spotted Dog', 'The Drunken Duck', 'The Pig and Whistle'....

slides.title: The Beatles
slides.titleZh: 乐坛神话 · 披头士乐队传奇
slides.tagline: 来自利物浦的四位年轻音乐人，如何用旋律改变整个世界！
slides.intro: 披头士（The Beatles）是世界流行音乐史上最伟大的摇滚乐队，他们的金曲至今在大街小巷传唱。
slides.contentEn:
John Lennon created this group, which was originally called 'The Quarrymen'. Lennon wrote most of the songs with Paul McCartney, and when George Harrison and Ringo Starr joined the group, the quartet was complete.
In 1961, Brian Epstein discovered the Beatles, and was convinced they would be a success. Their first single, released a year later, was called 'Love Me Do'. It was a modest hit, but great success followed. Indeed, their popularity was so great that the British press created a new word: 'Beatlemania'! The Beatles made two films, and had many number 1 singles. They were also the first group to make a music video.
One year after the release of the 'Abbey Road' album in 1969, the Beatles split up, and started solo careers. However, they remain the biggest-selling band in pop history, and still appeal to young and old alike.
slides.contentZh: 20世纪60年代，在英格兰西北部的工业港口城市利物浦，诞生了一支改写世界流行音乐历史的四人乐队——披头士（The Beatles）。由约翰·列侬、保罗·麦卡特尼、乔治·哈里森和林戈·斯塔尔组成的这支传奇乐团，凭借《Hey Jude》、《Yesterday》、《Let It Be》等一系列充满爱、和平与感染力的旋律风靡全球，掀起了著名的'披头士狂热'（Beatlemania）。他们的音乐不仅跨越国界与岁月，更成为跨世代无数青少年的精神灯塔。

quiz.question: Which city did the legendary Beatles come from? (传奇的披头士乐队来自哪座英国城市？)
quiz.explanation: 完全正确！披头士乐队来自英格兰著名的港口与音乐之都利物浦！

slides.title: Pantomimes
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 Pantomimes 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 探索英国及国际经典人文胜地，拓展少儿跨文化视野。
slides.contentEn:
It traditionally takes place during the Christmas season. The origins of the British Pantomime, or 'Panto' as it is known, date back to the Middle Ages. It has constantly been adapted to survive up to the present day.
The Pantomime as we know it today is predominantly for children and based on popular fairy tales such as 'Cinderella' or 'Aladdin'. The story line always involves good battling against evil and emerging triumphant. An important Pantomime character is the Dame, a comic role played by a man dressed in outrageous women's costumes. Audience participation is also an important part of Pantomime fun. The audience is often invited to dance and sing with the cast and when the villain appears behind the hero, children will shout as loud as they can 'He's behind you!'

slides.title: British Newspapers
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 British Newspapers 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 探索英国及国际经典人文胜地，拓展少儿跨文化视野。
slides.contentEn:
The first regular newspaper, 'The Daily Courant', appeared in 1702. It went out of circulation in 1735. 
The oldest national newspaper still in circulation is 'The Observer', which was created in 1791. This newspaper, only sold on Sundays, is called a broadsheet, as its pages are very large. Tabloid newspapers, such as 'The Sun' are smaller, and are often less serious. These newspapers prefer to focus on celebrities and gossip, rather than politics and world news. All British national newspapers, however, have political leanings. For example, 'The Times' is right wing, while 'The Guardian' is left wing.
It is difficult to imagine a day in Britain that doesn't start with a cup of tea and a read of a newspaper!

slides.title: British Cinema
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 British Cinema 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 探索英国及国际经典人文胜地，拓展少儿跨文化视野。
slides.contentEn:
The first film was produced in 1912. However, production stopped completely in 1924, because there was very little money invested in British cinema. A group of cinema enthusiasts, including Alfred Hitchcock, decided to revive the industry, and production restarted.
British cinema finally found its identity in the '50s and '60s. Ealing and Pinewood studios started to produce films with international appeal, such as 'The Ladykillers'. Certain films in the '60s, such as 'Alfie' or 'The Italian Job', both with Michael Caine, became immediate classics, and their style was undeniably British. The 'Carry On' films revived slapstick humour, while the James Bond films rivalled Hollywood for plot and action!
In the 1990s, films such as 'The Full Monty', starring Robert Carlyle, and 'Four Weddings and a Funeral' have received commercial and critical success, proving that the British film industry is as healthy as ever!

slides.title: British Food
slides.titleZh: 炸鱼与薯条 · 地道英式美味
slides.tagline: 外酥里嫩的金黄炸鱼，撒上海盐与麦醋，咬一口满嘴香脆！
slides.intro: Fish & Chips（炸鱼薯条）是英国无可争议的国民美食，早在维多利亚时代就是工人们的最爱！
slides.contentEn:
Traditional British cooking has created links with food from the countries of the former British Empire. Even today, it is not surprising that with such a multicultural society the variety of tastes and styles of cooking is phenomenal. In particular, Indian cuisine has become very popular throughout Britain thanks to the influence of the Indian community that has settled in Britain. Chicken tandoori and chicken tikka masala are two Indian dishes which are particularly popular in British homes. 
Amongst the more traditionally British meals, fish and chips is enjoyed throughout the nation, as is roast lamb and mint sauce, which is typically eaten on a Sunday. Do not forget the number of British culinary inventions that have been adopted worldwide, such as the sandwich which is possibly the most popular snack in the world! Equally, the English breakfast, the pub lunch, afternoon tea and picnics are all typically British!
slides.contentZh: 如果要选出最具代表性的英国国民美食，那绝对非'炸鱼薯条'（Fish & Chips）莫属！新鲜的大西洋鳕鱼（Cod）或黑线鳕（Haddock）裹上特调啤酒面糊，放入油锅炸至金黄酥脆，搭配粗切的金黄炸薯条。传统吃法一定要淋上几滴芬芳的麦醋（Malt Vinegar），撒上一撮海盐，配上一小碗甜甜的青豆泥（Mushy Peas）。在海风吹拂的英国海滨小镇，手捧一包热气腾腾的炸鱼薯条，是每个英国孩子最纯真的美味回忆！

quiz.question: What is traditionally sprinkled over British fish and chips? (英国传统吃法中常在炸鱼薯条上撒什么调味？)
quiz.explanation: 太赞啦！经典的英式吃法就是趁热撒上海盐和麦醋，酸香开胃、外酥里嫩！

slides.title: Sunday Roast
slides.titleZh: 星期天大餐 · 传统周日烤肉
slides.tagline: 周日家庭温馨大团圆，金黄约克郡布丁与香烤牛肉！
slides.intro: 周日烤肉大餐（Sunday Roast）是英国最温馨的家庭传统，一家人聚在一起分享香喷喷的烤肉与布丁。
slides.contentEn:
It is commonly eaten on Sunday afternoon, with vegetables, gravy and Yorkshire puddings. These are made with a pancake mixture cooked in the fat from the beef. If there is too much beef, it is often used for sandwiches for the next few days! Other common roasts include roast lamb, which often comes with a mint sauce, and roast pork, which goes very well with apple.

Wealthy newspaper publisher William Randolph Hearst wanted a dream home. This 'little something,' as he called it, was the magnificent Hearst Castle. Construction started in 1919, continuing until Hearst's death in 1951. 
Designed by American architect Julia Morgan, it was built at Camp Hill in the Santa Lucia Mountains overlooking San Simeon Bay. Hearst renamed the breathtaking site La Cuesta Encantada, 'The Enchanted Hill.' 
The estate's main house, 'Casa Grande,' was of Mediterranean Revival style with towers inspired by a Spanish cathedral. By the time it was finished, Hearst's dream home had 165 rooms, 127 acres of gardens, terraces, walkways and pools and one of the largest private art collections in the world! One of the pools, the Roman Pool, was even lined with Venetian glass and gold!
With such splendor, it's no surprise that Hearst Castle is often referred to as 'America's Castle!'

The U.S. owes this sandwich to the Germans. It was a German butcher who developed the frankfurter sausage in the Middle Ages. The frankfurter was also called a 'dachshund sausage,' as its shape was similar to that of the dachshund or hound dog.
In the 1860s, German immigrants in the U.S. began selling dachshund sausages in rolls with pickled cabbage or 'sauerkraut.' 
The name 'hot dog' came later. It is said that cartoonist Tad Dorgan invented the term when drawing a cartoon of a dachshund sausage seller. Dorgan could not spell 'dachshund' and wrote 'hot dog' in the caption instead.
Ever since, the hot dog has become an important part of U.S. culture.

On average, over two million people a year visit Yellowstone, making it one of America's most popular and fascinating natural wonders!

The director's first feature film was 'The Sugarland Express.' Released in 1974, this movie won the Cannes Film Festival Award for Best Screenplay. Many successful movies followed, including 'Jaws,' 'E.T.,' 'Jurassic Park' and the Indiana Jones series. In 1993, Spielberg won his first Best Picture Oscar for his World War II story 'Schindler's List.'
In 1994, Spielberg formed DreamWorks with two partners. This company produces films, TV shows, video games, computer software and music. Movies produced by DreamWorks include 'Saving Private Ryan.'
Today, the talented Spielberg is one of the big names in the U.S. movie industry.
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】史蒂文·斯皮尔伯格是美国当代最杰出的好莱坞导演与制片人之一。他执导的《大白鲨》、《E.T.》、《侏罗纪公园》、《夺宝奇兵》陪伴全球影迷成长，并凭借《辛德勒的名单》斩获奥斯卡最佳影片！

quiz.question: Which famous American movie was directed by Steven Spielberg? / 以下哪部世界著名经典电影是由斯皮尔伯格导演的？
options: The Lord of the Rings (指环王)
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！《侏罗纪公园》、《E.T.外星人》、《大白鲨》都是斯皮尔伯格执导的经典巨作！

slides.title: The Empire State Building
slides.titleZh: 环球探索 · The Empire State Building
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 The Empire State Building 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 帝国大厦傲立于纽约曼哈顿，拥有102层装饰艺术风格塔身，是纽约天际线的浪漫象征。
slides.contentEn:
Constructed between 1930 and 1932, this famous skyscraper is on the corner of Fifth Avenue and 34th Street on Manhattan Island. It is a quarter of a mile high and contains 102 floors. For forty years, it was the world's tallest building, until the Sears Tower was built in Chicago in 1973. 
Inside its graceful exterior, the Empire State Building is full of activity. It has many offices and shops, including restaurants and coffee bars.
For many, the Empire State Building, with its beautiful art deco architecture, symbolizes romance. It appears in many movies such as 'An Affair to Remember,' where a man played by Cary Grant waits at the top of the building for his lover played by Deborah Kerr. 
The Empire State Building is not just part of New York City's skyline, it is also part of its legend!
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】帝国大厦位于美国纽约市曼哈顿第五大道与第34街交界处，高102层，采用华丽的Art Deco（装饰艺术）风格，曾雄霸世界最高建筑长达40年，也是无数经典电影取景的浪漫地标！

quiz.question: Where is the Empire State Building located? / 帝国大厦位于哪个城市的曼哈顿岛？
options: New York City, USA (美国纽约)
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！帝国大厦是美国纽约市曼哈顿最著名的天际线地标！

slides.title: Elvis Presley
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 Elvis Presley 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 被誉为'猫王'的埃尔维斯·普雷斯利，开创了摇滚乐新时代，是20世纪美国流行文化符号。
slides.contentEn:
Elvis, better-known as 'the King,' was discovered in the early 1950s, and started recording for Sun Records. He was not an immediate success for Sun, but his unique style of music won many admirers. Blending blues, country and Tin Pan Alley ballads, his music became known as 'rockabilly.'
Colonel Tom Parker, who usually managed country musicians, became Elvis' manager in 1955, and made him a star. Elvis became an icon for America's youth, and dominated the charts. When he was drafted into the army in 1958, a nation believed it had lost its favorite star.
His return in 1960 proved this wrong. He continued hitting the charts, and made more than thirty movies! He defied the critics with a final No. 1 hit, 'Suspicious Minds,' in 1969.
Elvis died in 1977, but his legend lives on, and his following is as large as ever! He remains one of the largest influences on modern music.
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】'猫王'埃尔维斯·普雷斯利将布鲁斯蓝调、乡村音乐与流行民谣完美融合，掀起了全美乃至全球摇滚乐（Rock 'n' Roll）浪潮。他在乐坛与影坛创造了无数奇迹，是现代音乐史上极具影响力的传奇天王！

quiz.question: What nickname is American music legend Elvis Presley famously known as? / 美国传奇音乐家埃尔维斯·普雷斯利常被尊称为什么？
options: The King of Rock and Roll (摇滚之王 / 猫王)
The Prince of Pop (流行王子)
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！埃尔维斯·普雷斯利被尊称为'摇滚之王（The King）'，在中国也被亲切地称为'猫王'！

slides.title: Death Valley
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 Death Valley 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 位于加州与内华达州交界的死亡谷，拥有北美最低点恶水盆地和极其严苛的地貌气候。
slides.contentEn:
It covers over 3,000 square miles, but it is famous for its difficult weather conditions. Temperatures are very high. The highest temperature recorded was 134 °F, in 1913. There isn't much rain, either. The average yearly rainfall in Death Valley is just two inches!
The lowest point of the valley is at Badwater Basin. It is also the lowest point in the Western hemisphere, three hundred feet below sea level. The park's highest point is at Telescope Peak, in the Panamint Range Mountains. 
The Panamint Indians were the first to live in the valley. On Christmas Day, 1849, the Pioneers arrived, looking for a shortcut on their search for gold. They hadn't expected the hard conditions, and as they were leaving, they sang 'Good-bye Death Valley,' giving the area its name.
It is best to visit Death Valley in the winter, as conditions are only for the adventurous in the summer!
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】死亡谷国家公园位于美国加州东南部，占地超过3000平方英里。这里有西半球最低点——海平面下86米的恶水盆地（Badwater Basin），拥有极端高温与独特沙漠盐滩，是大自然最严酷而壮丽的景观！

quiz.question: What is the lowest point in Death Valley (and in North America) called? / 死亡谷中（也是北美洲）海拔最低的地点叫什么？
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！恶水盆地（Badwater Basin）海拔为海平面以下86米（282英尺），是北美洲最低点！

slides.title: The American Civil War
slides.titleZh: 环球探索 · The American Civil War
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 The American Civil War 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 1861至1865年的美国南北战争维护了国家统一，林肯总统发表了著名的《葛底斯堡演说》。
slides.contentEn:
The Civil War was between the Northern states and the Southern states. For many years, the two were held together by compromises, but the South had become dissatisfied. When Abraham Lincoln was elected President, several Southern states seceded from the Union, forming a new nation: the Confederacy.
The Confederate Army attacked on April 12th, 1861, starting the Civil War. For over two years, it looked likely that the Confederacy would win. The turning point came at the Battle of Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, in July, 1863. The Gettysburg Address, in which Lincoln declared the battlefield a National Cemetery, is one of the most celebrated speeches in U.S. history.
Lincoln was assassinated in 1865. He did not live to see the Confederate Army surrender in May of the same year, but he is celebrated as the leader who held the United States together.
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】美国南北战争（南北内战）发生在1861年至1865年。在亚伯拉罕·林肯总统领导下，联邦军队历经葛底斯堡战役等艰难转折，最终维护了美国国家的统一并废除了奴隶制，深刻塑造了现代美国。

quiz.question: Who was the U.S. President during the American Civil War? / 美国南北战争期间领导联邦的美国总统是谁？
options: Franklin D. Roosevelt (富兰克林·罗斯福)
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！亚伯拉罕·林肯在南北战争期间担任总统，坚决维护了国家统一并发表了《葛底斯堡演说》！

slides.title: The American Currency
slides.titleZh: 环球探索 · The American Currency
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 The American Currency 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 美元（US Dollar）是全球流通的重要货币，美国人常把美元俗称为'Bucks'，纸币印有建国先驱肖像。
slides.contentEn:
It is also the name of the currency in countries such as Australia, Canada and New Zealand. The dollar was introduced into the U.S. in 1792, and bills were first put into circulation in 1861.
The word 'dollar' originates from the German word 'Thaler.' It was created in the German town of Joachimsthal, and was the German currency until it was replaced by the Deutschmark in 1873.
Before 1792, the U.S. had many different currencies. In fact, in North Carolina in the 1770s, there were seventeen different forms of legal tender. These were all based on the British monetary system of pounds, shillings and pence. However, other currencies involved fur, rice and tobacco. Tobacco was used as currency in Virginia for over two hundred years!
Americans refer to dollars as 'bucks,' and money as 'dough.' Today, the American dollar is one of the strongest currencies in the world.
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】美元于1792年正式成为美国官方货币。美国人日常交流中常常把 dollar 亲切地称为 'bucks'（雄鹿皮演变而来），把钱叫做 'dough'。美元纸币与硬币记录着美国丰富的人文历史与建国先驱故事！

quiz.question: What informal slang word do Americans often use to refer to dollars? / 美国人在日常生活中常把'美元'称作什么俚语词？
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！美国人非常常用 'bucks' 来指代美元（例如 5 bucks 就是 5 美元）！

slides.title: J.F.K.
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 J.F.K. 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 第35任美国总统约翰·肯尼迪富有远见与演讲魅力，曾推动民权改革与阿波罗登月太空计划。
slides.contentEn:
J.F.K. was born in Brookline, Massachusetts, in 1917. He fought in the Pacific in World War II, and became a hero by saving his entire crew! After the war, he went into politics, and quickly made a name for himself.
While climbing the political ladder, he also became a writer. His book, 'Profiles in Courage,' won him the 1957 Pulitzer Prize. By 1960, J.F.K. was ready to run for the Presidency.
His victory over Richard Nixon in 1960 is mostly credited to his polished performances in front of TV cameras. As President, he focused on civil rights and international relations. However, his Presidency came to an abrupt end.
When J.F.K. was assassinated in November 1963, America lost perhaps its most popular President ever. He only spent just over a thousand days in office, but his impact was unprecedented, and his legacy will last forever.
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】约翰·肯尼迪（J.F.K.）出生于马萨诸塞州，是二战战斗英雄与普利策奖获奖作者，1960年当选美国第35任总统。虽然他在任仅有一千余天，但他倡导民权改革并开启阿波罗登月计划，留下了深远历史遗产！

quiz.question: Who was J.F.K. (John F. Kennedy)? / J.F.K.（约翰·肯尼迪）是哪国的著名总统？
options: The 35th President of the USA (美国第35任总统)
Prime Minister of the UK (英国首相)
Prime Minister of Canada (加拿大总理)
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！约翰·肯尼迪是美国历史上最受爱戴的总统之一，推动了民权和太空探索！

slides.title: George Gershwin
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 George Gershwin 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 乔治·格什温开创了将爵士乐融入交响乐的先河，《蓝色狂想曲》是美国音乐史上璀璨的瑰宝。
slides.contentEn:
Gershwin was born in Brooklyn, New York, in 1898. After leaving high school at fifteen, he worked as a pianist for a music publisher. He soon began writing music himself. Early in his career, Gershwin composed several instrumental pieces. 'Rhapsody in Blue,' with its famous clarinet solo, was one of these pieces. It was first performed in public in 1924.
The composer is also remembered for his ballads. He collaborated with his older brother Ira Gershwin, a lyric writer, on many of these. The brothers co-wrote twenty-two musical comedies. One of these, 'Of Thee I Sing,' was the first musical comedy to win a Pulitzer Prize. The brothers' most famous collaboration is perhaps 'Porgy and Bess.' This opera about poverty in a black community contains famous songs such as 'Summertime.'
George Gershwin died in 1937, but his songs have left a lasting influence on modern music.
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】乔治·格什温出生于纽约布鲁克林，他与作词家哥哥艾拉·格什温携手创作了无数经典。他的杰作《蓝色狂想曲》（Rhapsody in Blue）以著名的单簧管独奏惊艳世界，将美式爵士与古典交响完美相融！

quiz.question: Which famous musical piece was composed by American composer George Gershwin? / 以下哪首开创性的世界名曲是由美国作曲家乔治·格什温谱写的？
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！《蓝色狂想曲》（Rhapsody in Blue）是格什温将爵士乐融入古典音乐的传世杰作！

slides.title: Jackson Pollock
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 Jackson Pollock 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 抽象表现主义大师杰克逊·波洛克开创了'行动绘画'（滴画法），深刻改变了现代艺术走向。
slides.contentEn:
Born in Wyoming in 1912, he was encouraged to become an artist by his mother when he was young. Three of his five brothers also became artists. 
At seventeen, Pollock moved to New York City to study painting at the Art Students' League. Like his teacher, the famous painter Thomas Hart Benton, he began by painting rural scenes. 
Later, influenced by Native American sand painting, Pollock started to experiment with more abstract forms. By the late 1940s, he was known as an Abstract Expressionist painter.
Pollock developed the 'Action Painting' method. He fixed his canvas on the floor before putting paint onto it. Instead of using brushes, he used sticks or knives to paint forms. Sometimes, he stirred sand, glass or other materials into the paint. Like the Surrealist writers, Action painters believed that their movements reflected their unconscious moods.
American Abstract art owes its origins to Pollock.
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】杰克逊·波洛克出生于怀俄明州，后来在纽约开创了举世闻名的'行动绘画'（Action Painting）滴画技法。他把巨幅画布铺在地面，用木棍和颜料自然滴洒，开辟了美国抽象表现主义艺术的新纪元！

quiz.question: What revolutionary painting technique did American artist Jackson Pollock develop? / 美国艺术家杰克逊·波洛克开创了哪种极具革命性的绘画技法？
options: Action Painting / Drip technique (行动绘画 / 滴画法)
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！波洛克把画布铺在地上自由挥洒颜料，创造了闻名世界的'行动绘画'（Action Painting）！

slides.title: Martin Luther King Jr.
slides.titleZh: 环球探索 · Martin Luther King Jr.
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 Martin Luther King Jr. 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 民权领袖马丁·路德·金发表了震撼世界的《我有一个梦想》演说，倡导非暴力争取平等。
slides.contentEn:
Born in 1929, King led the Civil Rights Movement which helped to put an end to the segregation of African Americans in the U.S.
Like his father and maternal grandfather, he became a Baptist preacher. He obtained a doctorate in Theology at age twenty-six. His thesis was about the importance of faith. He believed that African Americans should use non-violent methods to obtain equality. He was influenced by the pacifist philosophy of Indian Prime Minister, Mohandas Gandhi.
In 1963, King led a large march to Washington, D.C., to protest against racism. Here, he gave his famous 'I have a dream' speech, where he expressed his hopes for the U.S.
Martin Luther King Jr. was tragically assassinated in 1968. In 1986, the U.S. Congress declared the third Monday in January a national holiday to commemorate King's birthday.
King died young at thirty-nine, but his work has had a lasting impact on American society.
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】马丁·路德·金是20世纪美国著名的民权运动领袖。1963年他在华盛顿林肯纪念堂前发表了举世闻名的《我有一个梦想》（I Have a Dream）演讲，倡导通过和平非暴力方式追求种族平等与正义！

quiz.question: What famous speech did Martin Luther King Jr. deliver in Washington, D.C. in 1963? / 1963年马丁·路德·金在华盛顿发表了哪篇举世闻名的历史演讲？
options: I Have a Dream (我有一个梦想)
Yes We Can (是的，我们能做到)
Blood, Toil, Tears and Sweat (热血、辛劳、眼泪与汗水)
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！马丁·路德·金发表了震撼全人类的《我有一个梦想》（I Have a Dream）演讲！

slides.title: The 1980s
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 The 1980s 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 20世纪80年代的美国经历了里根经济政策、科技腾飞与流行文化繁荣，自信心达到高潮。
slides.contentEn:
The defeat of Jimmy Carter signaled the start of a more conservative era in American politics. Reagan, a former film star and TV personality, inherited an economy in recession. He applied right-wing policies in order to reverse this.
He delivered tax cuts, deregulated the economy and reduced social welfare programs. Military spending increased enormously, largely due to the controversial 'Star-Wars' defense program. National debt rose to $4 trillion during Reagan's presidency. However, by the time he was re-elected in 1984, inflation had stopped rising, and American confidence was at an all-time high. 
On the international scene, Reagan will always be remembered for helping improve U.S.-Soviet relations. As the Cold War ended, he referred to Russian President Mikhail Gorbachev as his 'friend.'
When Reagan was replaced by Vice President George Bush in 1988, America was undoubtedly more confident, more powerful, and many Americans were certainly richer!
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】20世纪80年代是美国历史上极为耀眼的十年。在里根总统执政期间，美国推行减税与科技投资，冷战逐渐缓和，个人电脑与流行音乐席卷全球，全美社会迎来了前所未有的繁荣与自信！

quiz.question: Who served as the U.S. President throughout most of the 1980s? / 20世纪80年代大部分时间担任美国总统并深刻影响该时代的是谁？
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！罗纳德·里根在1981至1989年担任美国总统，是80年代美国政治与文化的核心人物！

slides.title: Amy Tan
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 Amy Tan 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 华裔女作家谭恩美以畅销小说《喜福会》享誉世界，生动展现了跨文化母女情深与寻根故事。
slides.contentEn:
Tan was born in 1952 to parents who came to the U.S. from China. She grew up in Oakland, California, where a large Chinese community lives. 
From 1981 to 1987, Tan worked as a technical writer, writing speeches and documents for business companies. However, she wanted a more creative career and started to write short stories.
In 1987, Tan traveled to China with her mother. When Tan was growing up, she had many conflicts with her mother. However, the trip to China changed Tan's attitude towards her. It also inspired her future novels.
Mother-daughter relationships are a theme of 'The Joy Luck Club,' Tan's first novel. Published in 1989, this international bestseller has been translated into seventeen languages. It was also made into a movie in 1993.
Tan has since written several novels and children's books. She continues to make important contributions to modern American literature.
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】谭恩美（Amy Tan）在加州奥克兰长大，是享誉国际的美国华裔当代作家。她的处女作《喜福会》（The Joy Luck Club）生动描绘了华裔移民两代母女的文化碰撞与深沉亲情，被翻译成多种语言并改编为经典电影！

quiz.question: What is the title of Amy Tan's famous bestselling novel exploring mother-daughter relationships? / 谭恩美探讨华人移民母女情感与跨文化成长的著名畅销小说叫什么？
options: To Kill a Mockingbird (杀死一只知更鸟)
The Great Gatsby (了不起的盖茨比)
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！《喜福会》（The Joy Luck Club）是谭恩美轰动全球的畅销代表作！

slides.title: Silicon Valley
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 Silicon Valley 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 坐落于加州的硅谷是全球高科技与互联网创新的心脏，诞生了数千家改变世界的科技巨头。
slides.contentEn:
Silicon Valley, otherwise known as the Santa Clara Valley, is in California. Prunes and apricots are not as common as they once were, because this valley has been taken over by companies creating computer hardware and Internet technology. There are over three thousand high-tech companies in Silicon Valley, many of which are very new!
One of the oldest companies in Silicon Valley was started in 1939. William Hewlett and David Packard were students at the nearby Stanford University. Their professor, Fred Terman, encouraged them to start their own business. The resulting company, Hewlett-Packard, now employs over 100,000 people across the world, and is one of Silicon Valley's many success stories!
While the soil in Silicon Valley may be good for growing fruit, today it is the companies in the valley that are bearing fruit!
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】硅谷位于美国加州圣克拉拉山谷，毗邻斯坦福大学。从早期的惠普（HP）车库创业，到如今聚集着超过三千家顶级高科技与互联网企业，这里孕育了芯片、操作系统与人工智能，是全球科技创新的灯塔！

quiz.question: Where is Silicon Valley, the global center of high-tech innovation, located? / 全球高科技创新中心'硅谷'位于美国的哪一个州？
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！硅谷位于美国加利福尼亚州旧金山湾区南部，是全球顶尖科技企业的大本营！

slides.title: 'Teddy' Roosevelt and the Bear Cub
slides.titleZh: 环球探索 · 'Teddy' Roosevelt and the Bear Cub
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 'Teddy' Roosevelt and the Bear Cub 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 泰迪熊的名字源于美国第26任总统西奥多·罗斯福拒绝伤害小熊的温情历史轶事。
slides.contentEn:
It is called the 'Teddy Bear' thanks to America's 26th President, Theodore Roosevelt, who was nicknamed 'Teddy.' In 1906, Roosevelt went on a hunting trip. He was accompanied by many aides and reporters. For days, the reporters wrote stories about Roosevelt's hunting failures. The aides decided to help, and captured a bear cub for Roosevelt to shoot. When he refused, the reporters had a story.
A cartoon, drawn by cartoonist Clifford Berryman, appeared in the Washington Post. It showed Roosevelt refusing to shoot a bear cub. Inspired by this cartoon, toy shop owners Rose and Morris Michlom made a small toy bear. They put it in the shop window with the sign 'Teddy's Bear.' It was so popular that they formed the 'Ideal Novelty & Toy' company to market the Teddy Bear.
Today, almost every child has a Teddy Bear, but not many know that the original Teddy was an American President!
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】深受全世界小朋友喜爱的毛绒玩偶'泰迪熊'（Teddy Bear），名字源自美国第26任总统西奥多·'泰迪'·罗斯福！1906年打猎时他拒绝向一只被捕获的小黑熊开枪，《华盛顿邮报》刊登漫画后，玩具店制作了'泰迪的小熊'，从此风靡全球！

quiz.question: Which American President inspired the name of the 'Teddy Bear'? / 小朋友们喜爱的'泰迪熊'（Teddy Bear）的名字来源于哪位美国总统？
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！'Teddy Bear'得名于美国第26任总统西奥多·罗斯福的小名'Teddy'！

slides.title: County and State Fairs
slides.titleZh: 环球探索 · County and State Fairs
slides.tagline: 跟着小狮子敢敢，探索世界名胜 County and State Fairs 的精彩故事！
slides.intro: 郡博览会与州博览会是美国热闹的传统节庆，集农牧评比、吃馅饼比赛、游乐嘉年华于一体。
slides.contentEn:
These fairs often last several days, and they are mostly agricultural. They are an opportunity for people from the city to see country life. It is also a chance for rural communities to get together and celebrate.
If you go to a County Fair, you can see lots of competitions. There are competitions for the best flower, best vegetable, or even the biggest vegetable. The winner gets a blue ribbon, and of course, their photo in the local newspaper. Other kinds of competitions include the pie-eating contest, where the winner is the person who eats the most pie.
State Fairs are often a lot bigger than County Fairs. People come from all over the state and stay at campsites. There are fairground attractions, concerts, and let's not forget the competitions!
County and State Fairs are typical American events that are lots of fun!
slides.contentZh: 【敢敢导览】郡博览会（County Fair）和州博览会（State Fair）是美国最具特色的传统民俗盛会！人们在这里展示自家最大的南瓜、评选冠军蓝丝带蔬菜、举行趣味吃馅饼比赛，并尽情体验摩天轮与嘉年华游乐设施，充满了欢声笑语！

quiz.question: In typical American county and state fairs, what award does the winner often receive for the best produce? / 在美国典型的郡县或州博览会农产品竞赛中，获奖优胜者通常会获得什么标志性奖励？
quiz.explanation: 太棒啦！在美国博览会比赛中，第一名优胜者通常会获得著名的'蓝丝带（blue ribbon）'！
